sourceEvidence.claim: Virulence block (cord factor — serpentine cord, macrophage activation, granuloma formation, TNF-α release; sulfatides inhibit phagolysosomal fusion)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Cord factor creates a “serpentine cord”
appearance in virulent M tuberculosis
strains; activates macrophages (promoting
granuloma formation) and induces release of
TNF-α. Sulfatides (surface glycolipids) inhibit
phagolysosomal fusion.

sourceEvidence.claim: PPD/IGRA rules (PPD ⊕ current/past infection or BCG; PPD ⊝ no infection and immunocompromised with low CD4+; IGRA fewer BCG false positives)
sourceEvidence.quote:
PPD ⊕ if current/past infection (or BCG
vaccination).
PPD ⊝ if no infection and in
immunocompromised patients (especially with
low CD4+ cell count).
Interferon-γ release assay (IGRA) has fewer false
positives from BCG vaccination.

sourceEvidence.claim: The histology rule (caseating granulomas with central necrosis and Langhans giant cell with inline photo marker A; do not confuse Langhans giant cell [fused macrophages] with Langerhans cell [dermal APC])
sourceEvidence.quote:
Caseating granulomas with central necrosis and
Langhans giant cell (single example in A )
are characteristic of 2° tuberculosis. Do not
confuse Langhans giant cell (fused
macrophages) with Langerhans cell (dermal
APC).

sourceEvidence.claim: The reactivation rule (risk highest in immunocompromised: HIV, organ transplant recipients, TNF-α inhibitor use; apices of the lung — highly aerobic)
sourceEvidence.quote:
TB reactivation risk highest in
immunocompromised individuals (eg, HIV,
organ transplant recipients, TNF-α inhibitor
use). Reactivation has a predilection for the
apices of the lung (due to the bacteria being
highly aerobic).

sourceEvidence.claim: Leprosy entry part 1 (Hansen disease; M leprae acid-fast bacillus, cool temperatures, skin and superficial nerves with 'glove and stocking' loss, cannot be grown in vitro; dx skin biopsy or tissue PCR; US reservoir armadillos; the two forms with ▘ bullet glyphs — lepromatous [diffuse, leonine facies with inline photo marker A, communicable, high bacterial load, low CMI largely Th2, can be lethal] vs tuberculoid [few hypoesthetic hairless plaques with inline photo marker B, high CMI largely Th1, low bacterial load]; 'cellmediated' hyphen-drop quoted as printed)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Also called Hansen disease. Caused by Mycobacterium leprae, an acid-fast bacillus that likes cool
temperatures (infects skin and superficial nerves—“glove and stocking” loss of sensation) and
cannot be grown in vitro. Diagnosed via skin biopsy or tissue PCR. Reservoir in United States:
armadillos.
Leprosy has 2 forms (many cases fall temporarily between two extremes):
▘ Lepromatous—presents diffusely over the skin, with leonine (lionlike) facies A , and is
communicable (high bacterial load); characterized by low cell-mediated immunity with a
largely Th2 response. Lepromatous form can be lethal.
▘ Tuberculoid—limited to a few hypoesthetic, hairless skin plaques B ; characterized by high cellmediated immunity with a largely Th1 response and low bacterial load.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Leprosy treatment rule (dapsone and rifampin for tuberculoid; clofazimine added for lepromatous)
sourceEvidence.quote: Treatment: dapsone and rifampin for tuberculoid form; clofazimine is added for lepromatous form.

kypExtensions.summary: The immune-gate reading of the spectrum (every outcome is a cell-mediated verdict: the >90% road is the competent Th1 host, reactivation is the wall's guards going down [HIV, transplant, TNF-α inhibitors — the drugs that block the very cytokine cord factor induces], and the <10% road is the never-competent host); the leprosy pole as the same axis printed as a skin disease (E31's IL-12/IFN-γ circuit); the lobe-assignment rule (mid/lower primary focus vs apical reactivation — the aerobic-preference contrast); the anergy reading of a negative PPD; and the miliary organ list as Pott/adrenal exam cross-links — labeled as integrations.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the flowchart, rules, and entries without the immune-axis synthesis or the cross-chapter wiring; these integrations are KYP's design.
